approach: Add a first-in-first-out landing queue to `Drain` (drain.rs). A worker joins it when its run passes, keeps its place through the landing retry, and leaves on every exit through a drop guard. Only the queue head lands. Before `Steps::land`, the head gets a rebase check from a new `Steps::rebase` (default: clean). In production it calls a new `Athena::rebase_for_landing` in landing.rs. That fetches origin's main and uses a pure `plan_rebase` to replay the local branch onto it with `Git::replay`. A clean move rebuilds the local branch with `reset_keep`, so the existing `land_pr` and `replace_early` path pushes the rebased landing commit. The result maps to a drain-side `Rebased` through a small pure function, `rebased_from`. A conflicting candidate is held back (not landed, main untouched, no retry, not a stop) and the next queued candidate lands. Return to the producer and the thrash stop are left to A6b. Today's `[parallel] max_concurrency` > 1 path already lands later group jobs (see decision 1); it stays as it is and is pinned by a test.

decisions.choice: Today's landing of the second job of a group, which the producer writes into a code comment at `Drain::land` and into async-drain.md: it lands, and the queue must keep that. Local landing (`land_or_block`, crates/athena-core/src/run/close.rs:226-315, using `land::plan`, land.rs:37-87) rebuilds each job's verified candidate on the current local branch tip under the repository lock. It is Stale only when governed content changed. The second job's landing commit therefore sits on top of the first job's. After the first job's pull request merges, `Athena::after_merge` (landing.rs:556) calls `resync_onto_merge` (land.rs:190), which uses `resync_tip` (land.rs:99) to replay the later local commits onto the host's merge commit. By the time the second job reaches `land_pr`, main is already an ancestor of its landing commit, so the new rebase returns `Rebase::Current` and nothing changes.
decisions.reason: This answers finding 1. The queue's rebase only acts when main moved in a way the resync did not cover (an outside push, or a first job that was not landed). A real-git test pins the claim (`resync_tip` then `plan_rebase` gives `Current`). A `drain_concurrent` test with max_concurrency 2 pins that both jobs of a group land one at a time with the second rebase check after the first landing.

rejected.option: Treat any job whose base is not the latest main as needing a rebase and re-check
rejected.why: It would turn the second group job into 'not landed' although it lands today.
The reading says with max_in_flight = 1 the drain behaves as today, and that includes max_concurrency > 1.

decisions.choice: The queue slot belongs to the item. `attempts` creates a `QueueSlot` drop guard (item.job pushed to `State.queue`) on `RunStep::Passed`, keeps it across the landing retry loop, and drops it on every return. `Drain::land` waits (using `pause`) until its item is the queue head, then takes the existing `landing` mutex. Waiters do not check `stopped()`: the head always finishes, and the guard releases on panic too.
decisions.reason: The retry in `attempts` calls `land` twice for one pass, and the existing test `a_landing_failure_is_a_failure_and_no_rating_is_taken_as_success` pins `[read a, run a, land a, land a]`. A slot dropped after one `land` call would hang the second. The `landing` mutex serialises but does not order. Not checking `stopped()` means a verified job is still landed after a stop request, as today.

rejected.option: Dequeue at the end of every `Drain::land` call
rejected.why: The second landing attempt of the same pass would wait for itself.
Waiters wake in no fixed order, so queue order would not be guaranteed.

rejected.option: Waiters give up when a stop is requested
rejected.why: It would abandon a verified job that lands today.

decisions.choice: Rebase result is a typed value in landing.rs: `Rebase { Current, Moved{onto,tip}, NeedsRecheck{onto}, Conflict{onto,text}, Unchecked(String) }`. The pure `plan_rebase(git, onto, head, landed, rules_commit, verified_fp, sign) -> Result<Rebase>` does: `Current` if `onto` is an ancestor of `landed`; otherwise fork = merge-base(onto, head); an error (not a conflict) if a first-parent commit of fork..head has no parent; `Git::replay(onto, fork, head, sign)`; a `GitError::Refused` from replay becomes `Conflict` with its text; on a clean replay, compare `athena_git::attrs::fingerprint(git, tip, rules_commit)` with `verified_fp`. Equal gives `Moved`, different gives `NeedsRecheck`, and nothing moves.
decisions.reason: This reuses `replay` (athena-git lib.rs:773), the primitive `resync_tip` already uses. The fingerprint check is needed because the fingerprint covers the whole governed tree: a rebased tree whose governed content differs was not verified, and the merge's content check would reject it after the push. Re-checking after a rebase is build job 7, so NeedsRecheck is reported as not landed and names job 7. The parent pre-check keeps replay's 'has no parent' refusal from being reported as a conflict.

rejected.option: Push the rebased head without the fingerprint check
rejected.why: It would merge content Athena did not verify.

rejected.option: Match the conflict by error text only
rejected.why: Fragile against wording changes; the pre-check separates the non-conflict refusal.

rejected.option: Compute conflicting file names with merge-tree --name-only
rejected.why: Paths are only needed by the producer return in A6b; the replay text names the commit and base.

decisions.choice: `Athena::rebase_for_landing(job_ref, runner, ui) -> Result<Rebase>` resolves the job as `land_pr` does. It returns `Unchecked(reason)` when origin is missing or not a supported remote, the default branch cannot be read (`PrHost::default_branch`), `Git::fetch_remote_branch` fails or finds nothing, or the job has no landed commit on the branch (`land_pr` then goes its own way, including `confirm_existing_merge`). After a good fetch it takes `lock_repository`, re-reads head, runs `plan_rebase`, and on `Moved` calls `reset_keep(tip)` and prints one line. A refused `reset_keep` or any other error after the fetch is an `Err`.
decisions.reason: Today's `land_pr` does no fetch before landing. A short network failure must not become 'not landed' where it lands today. The skipped check is shown as one warning line instead.

rejected.option: Treat a failed fetch as Blocked
rejected.why: It changes today's behavior on a network failure.
`resync_onto_merge` takes it for the same branch rewrite, so the rebase must too.

decisions.choice: The mapping is a pure function in drain.rs, `rebased_from(Result<Rebase>) -> Rebased`, with `Rebased { Clean(Option<String>), Conflict{onto,text}, Blocked(String) }`. Current and Moved give `Clean(None)`; `Unchecked(why)` gives `Clean(Some(warning))`; `NeedsRecheck` gives `Blocked` naming build job 7; `Conflict` gives `Conflict`; `Err` gives `Blocked`. `PrLander::rebase` is `rebased_from(athena.rebase_for_landing(job, &GhCli, ui))`. `Drain::land` prints the warning as one `ui.line` and lands.
decisions.reason: This answers finding 3: each arm is unit-tested without a network or a repository, and a Drain-level test shows the warning prints once and the job still lands.

rejected.why: It needs a live Athena and a remote to test.

decisions.choice: A conflicting candidate is held back, not returned. `Drain::land` returns a new `LandStep::Conflict`; `attempts` sets the job line's landing to 'held back: rebase conflict ...', does not retry, and ends the item as a new `ItemEnd::Conflicted`. `finish` passes the item over ('held back: ...') and sets no stop. The slot is released, so the next queued candidate lands. `Rebased::Blocked` follows the existing NotLanded path (one failure, one retry). The held-back item stays as it is: locally landed, pull request unmerged, as after any NotLanded today. A6b adds the return to the producer.
decisions.reason: A retry would only conflict again. Counting a conflict as a failure would reach `ATTEMPTS` twice and set `Stop::RepeatedFailure`, which ends the whole drain and contradicts 'the next candidate still lands'. Items handed to a worker are recorded in `State.tried` (the producer confirms in `batches_for`, drain.rs ~2215), so a held-back item is not offered again in a later wave. A test asserts that no second `rebase` or `land` call for it follows.

rejected.why: A pointless retry, and two conflicts stop the whole drain.
It stops other candidates from landing.

decisions.choice: One extra line in crates/athena-core/src/gh/mod.rs: add `plan_rebase` and `Rebase` to the existing `pub use landing::{...}` list (gh/mod.rs:51).
decisions.reason: `landing` is a private module (gh/mod.rs:37), so athena-cli cannot name the new items otherwise. It is code, not governance, but is not in the expected deliverables, so it is flagged in open questions.

rejected.why: It would lose the typed arms that the pure mapping and its tests rely on.

risks.risk: Changing `Drain::land` and `attempts` alters the serial path that existing tests pin, notably the landing retry.
risks.mitigation: The slot is held by the item through the retry loop, so a single worker is head on both `land` calls. All new trait methods default to clean, and `Current` is returned when main is already in the landed commit's history. Criterion 5 runs the existing suite and checks the diff for removed lines.

risks.risk: A queue slot left behind by a panic, budget end or early return blocks the workers behind it.
risks.mitigation: `QueueSlot` is a drop guard that removes the item and notifies, and `pause` wakes every 20 ms. A holder goes straight from taking the slot to `land`, so it never waits on a later worker.

risks.risk: A rebase that moves the branch could make the existing `land_pr` refuse, because the remote head is no longer the job's early head, or `reset_keep` could be refused by local edits.
risks.mitigation: A refused `reset_keep` is an Err and leaves the branch unchanged; it maps to `Blocked`, the normal 'not landed' path with its reason shown. `replace_early` and its guard are reused unchanged. The risk is named in the design doc.

risks.risk: A real queue with several jobs in flight will often see governed changes from another job's landing, so rebased jobs come back as NeedsRecheck (not landed) until build job 7.
risks.mitigation: Reported as not landed with a reason naming job 7; nothing is pushed or merged. The follow-up job removes it. At max_in_flight = 1 each job is built on the latest main, so the fingerprint matches.

risks.risk: The order test cannot prove the FIFO against a non-fair mutex.
risks.mitigation: The head's `land` is gated so the others pile up, and the scenario repeats 10 times with different arrival orders. This makes a non-FIFO implementation fail very likely (an estimate), and the report says so.

risks.risk: A held-back job stays locally landed with its pull request unmerged, and a later drain's view of it is not settled.
risks.mitigation: It is the same state as after any NotLanded today. It is recorded in the design doc and handled in A6b.

risks.risk: A fetch of origin's main in tests or in a drain with no network.
risks.mitigation: A failure gives `Unchecked`: one warning line and landing goes on as today. The core tests use a local repository as 'origin', or call `plan_rebase` directly.

risks.risk: New code trips `-D warnings` (dead code, unused default-method parameters).
risks.mitigation: Prefix unused default-method parameters with `_`, read every new variant in production code, add no `#[allow]`, and run clippy before finishing.

demonstrations.method: Two layers. (a) A drain test through the production entry point `drain::drain_concurrent(&world, limits(9.0), &Quiet, 3)`. Preconditions: three items a, b, c in one batch (the `independent` helper: disjoint touched paths, no dependencies), bound 3, budget room. Seam: a new Sync `QueueWorld` in a new `mod landing_queue` appended at the end of tests/drain.rs, implementing the real `Steps` trait (the `parallel::Shared` stub at tests/drain.rs:5117 shows the style). Its `run` is gated with Mutex and Condvar so verification ends in the order c, a, b although items start a, b, c. Its `land` for c blocks on a gate until a and b have both passed their run and are waiting, so they pile up behind the head. `rebase` logs 'rebase X onto main-N' and returns `Rebased::Clean(None)`; `land` logs 'land X' and bumps N. The queue, head wait and the rebase call are in `Drain`, not in the double. The scenario repeats 10 times with different gate orders. A second test, `landing_queue_landing_retry_keeps_its_place`, makes the head's first `land` fail once and asserts the log `land a, land a, land c` within a bounded wait. This seam does not exist today; step 6 adds it. (b) Core tests on a real temporary git repository, using the helper style of the `resync_tip` tests in crates/athena-core/src/land.rs (~383-526): three job branches each cut from the same old base with one landing commit (trailers kept), main advanced as a queue would. For each in queue order: `plan_rebase(onto = current main tip, ...)` gives `Moved`; its tip's parent equals the current main tip, trailers and message are kept and the fingerprint equals the verified one; main then advances to the tip. Finally `git rev-list --merges` is empty and `git log --first-parent` lists the three landings in queue order. Also a records-only move of main gives `Moved`, a governed move gives `NeedsRecheck` with the branch untouched, and main already in the landed commit's history gives `Current`.
demonstrations.command: cargo test --locked -p athena-cli --test drain landing_queue_lands && cargo test --locked -p athena-cli --test drain landing_queue_landing_retry && cargo test --locked -p athena-core plan_rebase
demonstrations.observes: (a) The log shows 'land' entries in verified order c, a, b, never overlapping. Each 'rebase X onto main-N' follows the previous 'land', with N rising by one per landing. `report.landed` has 3 entries. The retry test finishes inside its bound. (b) The three rebased tips form one line on main, with no merge commits, in queue order. `NeedsRecheck` leaves the branch tip as it was.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the queue, a and b wake in the mutex's order, and the repeated pile-up scenario breaks the c, a, b assertion (a probabilistic check, not a proof: std's mutex is not fair, but order is not guaranteed). Without the rebase call the 'rebase X onto main-N' lines are missing. If the slot is dropped after one `land` call, the retry test hangs and fails on its bounded wait. Without `plan_rebase` the core tests do not compile or fail on the parent and linear-history assertions.

demonstrations.method: Two layers. (a) `landing_queue_conflict_is_held_back_and_the_next_candidate_lands` through `drain::drain_concurrent` with `QueueWorld`: the `rebase` of b returns `Rebased::Conflict{onto:"main-1", text}`, and a, c are clean. The gate piles b, then c, behind a. Seam: `Steps::rebase`, the default method added in step 4; `QueueWorld` is added in step 6. (b) A core test `plan_rebase_conflict_changes_nothing` on a real temporary repository: two commits change the same line, one on main and one on the job's landing commit. `plan_rebase` returns `Rebase::Conflict` (not `Err`). The main ref and the branch tip are the same before and after. A second case, a landing commit that has a root (parentless) commit in its range, is an `Err` and not a `Conflict`.
demonstrations.command: cargo test --locked -p athena-cli --test drain landing_queue_conflict && cargo test --locked -p athena-core plan_rebase_conflict
demonstrations.observes: (a) The log has 'rebase b' but no 'land b'; main's counter does not advance for b; 'land c' follows 'land a'. b is called once, with no retry rebase or land, and no later wave works it again. b's job line landing starts with 'held back: rebase conflict'. `report.stop` is not `RepeatedFailure`, and `report.landed` lists a and c. (b) Conflict result with a replay text naming the commit; refs unchanged; the parentless case is an Err.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the conflict branch the stubbed Conflict is ignored and 'land b' is logged, so the first assertion fails. If a conflict is counted as a failure, b is retried (a second 'rebase b' appears) and the stop reason becomes `RepeatedFailure`, which fails the test. Without the replay-to-Conflict mapping, the core test gets an `Err` or a `Moved` instead.

demonstrations.method: A drain test `landing_queue_max_concurrency_2_lands_both_jobs_of_a_group_one_at_a_time` through `drain::drain_concurrent(&world, limits(9.0), &Quiet, 2)` with two independent items in the same batch (the `independent` helper) and `QueueWorld` using the default clean `rebase`. Plus a core test `second_group_job_is_current_after_the_first_merge`: a real temporary repository holds job 1's and job 2's local landing commits on one branch; a squash commit of job 1 is made on main; `resync_tip` (land.rs:99, the production function `resync_onto_merge` calls) rebuilds the branch; then `plan_rebase` for job 2 returns `Current`. The producer writes the answer of decision 1, with the file and line numbers, as a comment on `Drain::land` and in async-drain.md.
demonstrations.command: cargo test --locked -p athena-cli --test drain landing_queue_max_concurrency_2 && cargo test --locked -p athena-core second_group_job_is_current
demonstrations.observes: Both jobs land (`report.landed` has 2 entries); the log shows 'rebase second' only after 'land first' ended; peak runs in flight is 2 while landings never overlap. The core test shows the second job's landing is `Current`, so the new rebase changes nothing on today's group path.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the queue or rebase made the second group job not land (for example by treating a base that is not the latest main as NeedsRecheck), `report.landed` would hold 1 entry and the first test fails. If `plan_rebase` replayed a branch whose main is already an ancestor, the core test would get `Moved` instead of `Current`.
